chapter: Kid Rena, Kelly and the old trumpeters
title: Perez's powerful sound, his band and Pythian roof garden
summary: Perez could be heard blocks away; his band played the Pythian Temple roof garden, one of the first places Justin listened alone.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: You could hear him by three or four blocks. And everything he played was so clear and concise I mean you could hear everything he blew.
Do you remember the name of his band?
Well I think at that time they used to call his band the Excelsas.

I think that's what it was because they used to have about seven or eight piece units. And I think he used to play for various engagements I think when the old roof garden was in prominence a long time ago. And that's one of the first places I ever- Gravier? That's right. Right there on Gravier. The Pitian Temple.
The old Pitian Temple. Still there.
They call it the Civic Center building. They tore all that part down. Yes I heard about it. The City Hall was right there across there.
Well that was one of the first spots I did get a chance to listen to when I was able to get out by myself.
And Manuel Perez played up there.

Yeah. Sometimes I even went out there with relatives. To have a social affair I'd get up there and of course most of my time was spent on the bandstand. I never cared too much about dancing but I just loved to listen to the music and try to find out to see what was going on. And of course at that time, at that particular time they had several fellas that I used to think were some of the greatest musicians I had ever heard in my life of course.
